Hi Naomi —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As part of HelixGuard's security RFP and the EU DPF assessment our legal team is compiling a tighter set of technical and operational evidence. We wanted to capture a single-thread with clear answers so our procurement and infosec reviewers can sign off. Below are the immediate asks — if you can share a short written response plus any artifacts it would be ideal.

1) Which lawful transfer mechanism do you rely on when processing HelixGuard EU personal data in third countries? Please list the standard contractual clauses (SCCs) version and whether you offer DPA annexes tailored for controllers.
2) Key management: do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) in hosted mode? If yes, which KMS providers and supported key rotation/rotation windows?
3) Subprocessor controls: current subprocessor roster for EU data + process for notification and objection.
4) Audit logs & retention: what logs are retained, retention windows, and how are they delivered for audits?
5) Data residency options and private deployment playbook if HelixGuard requires on-prem or VPC-only processing.
6) Any recent transfer-risk assessments or DPF mapping documents you can provide.

We'd appreciate anything you can provide by Monday 12/20. If it helps we can do a 30-minute technical deep dive.

Best,
Sophie Lam
Head of Security Programs, HelixGuard

Hi Sophie and team —

Appreciate the detailed asks. Below are concise answers and references; please let me know if you want deeper artifacts for any bullet. I've attached a detailed subprocessor roster and a DPA annex draft for HelixGuard (redwood_subprocessors_2027.csv, dpa-annex-helixguard-redwood-v1.docx).

1) Lawful transfer mechanism
- Default mechanism for hosted Redwood customers: European Commission 2021 Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), controllers-to-processor flow. We provide an SCC addendum in our DPA annex; the annex includes specific subprocessors and transfer pathways.
- For customers requiring additional safeguards we offer: Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) and Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) to avoid transfers to third countries.

2) Key management (BYOK)
- Hosted: We support customer-managed keys in hosted mode using AWS KMS and Google Cloud KMS (customer-project keys) for encryption at rest and envelope encryption. Customers can supply keys via KMS grants or use our HSM integration for dedicated/private deployments.
- Rotation: key rotation can be scheduled by customer; we recommend rotation windows of 30–90 days. We do not forcibly rotate customer-managed keys; operational rotation policies remain customer-controlled.

3) Subprocessor controls
- Current EU-impacting subprocessors (summary): AWS (eu-west-1/3), Google Cloud (europe-west), FastStorage CDN, LogArchive Inc. (log retention). Full CSV attached.
- Notification process: We notify customers 30 days prior to onboarding a new subprocessor for EU data. Customers have the option to object per DPA; objection escalates to a mitigation plan or Private deployment if needed.

4) Audit logs & retention
- Types of logs: request-level access logs (per API key), model invocation traces (no raw PII unless explicitly logged by customer), admin config changes, and infra-level audit events.
- Retention windows: default 90 days for request and invocation logs; 365 days for admin/audit trail (config changes). We can extend retention to meet contractual requirements as an add-on.
- Delivery: logs are delivered via secure S3 export or shared audit bundle (encrypted) for in-scope audits; we support read-only auditor access under NDA.

5) Data residency & private deployment
- Options: Hosted (multi-region), Dedicated (tenant-isolated GPU pools in specified region), Private (VPC or on-prem appliance). Private includes an installation runbook, network requirements, and optional on-prem package for air-gapped operation.
- Playbook: we will provide a runbook with network flow diagrams, minimum instance types, and onboarding checklist (we can provide an example during the technical call).

6) Transfer-risk assessments / DPF mapping
- Attached is a 20-page mapping extract in the summary pack. We also run a transfer-risk checklist aligned to EDPB guidance for non-adequate countries and can produce a HelixGuard-specific supplement upon request.

Additional notes:
- Certifications: SOC 2 Type II (infra & cloud controls) and ISO 27001 certified for our core platform.
- Encryption in transit: TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers; we also support mutual TLS for Private deployments.
- SLA/assurance: Dedicated customers receive SLA of 99.9% availability and per-route latency targets; hosted customers have published performance profiles.

If you'd like, I can prepare a short artifact bundle for each area — SCC excerpts, KMS integration notes, auditor-access template, and the full subprocessor CSV — and share them before the call.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Compliance & Trust
Redwood Inference
